evals.prompt: I just ran chezmoi add --encrypt ~/.config/zsh/.work.env after adding a new GITHUB_TOKEN. Before I commit, make sure the token isn't sitting in plaintext anywhere.
evals.expected_output: Triggers the skill. Runs scripts/verify_encrypted.sh ~/.config/zsh/.work.env. Reports the source is encrypted_dot_work.env.age with an age header, chezmoi cat round-trips, and the working-tree + git-history + template scans are clean (auto-derived secret values, or --expect-value 'ghp_...' if the user names the token). Ends with PASS = safe to commit, or FAIL with the exact file/commit if the token leaked.

evals.prompt: i think i messed up — encrypted dot_env.tmpl but when i cat it the .tmpl still shows my actual API keys. did i leak them?
evals.expected_output: Triggers the skill. Explains the Trap-2 root cause: a .tmpl is rendered, never decrypted, so an inline literal secret is plaintext in the source and git. Runs verify_encrypted.sh with --expect-value for the leaked keys; the template scan (check 6) flags the .tmpl, and the history scan flags it if already committed. Directs the user to move the secret into an encrypted_ non-template (or reference it at render time), rotate the keys (compromised), and re-verify.

evals.prompt: Add my new Anthropic API key as a chezmoi secret and prove it never hits the repo in plaintext. Key goes in ~/.config/zsh/.env.
evals.expected_output: Triggers the skill. Walks the add flow: write plaintext to ~/.config/zsh/.env at the target, run chezmoi add --encrypt ~/.config/zsh/.env (matches the existing encrypted_dot_env.age source), then run scripts/verify_encrypted.sh ~/.config/zsh/.env --expect-value 'sk-ant-...'. Confirms encrypted_ + .age, age header, round-trip, and clean working-tree/history/template scans before advising commit.

should_not_trigger: Preview what chezmoi apply would change and check none of my templates are broken before I apply. (This is general template-render / dry-run verification — route to the chezmoi-verify skill, not the secret encrypt+leak-proof flow.)

Decrypt ~/.config/zsh/.work.env so I can read my current GITHUB_TOKEN value out loud. (This is a plain read/decrypt for use, not adding/rotating a secret or proving no leak — `chezmoi cat` or `chezmoi decrypt` directly; the verifier masks values and never prints them.)
Rotate the IAM access keys in our Terraform tfvars and update the AWS SSO profile. (Cloud-credential rotation in an infra/terraform repo, nothing to do with chezmoi age-encrypted dotfile entries.)
